text:
Maya Patel: Hey team — drafting a per-route escalation matrix PR for the console SLOs. Goal: reduce noisy pages from low-severity routes while preserving fast escalation for critical paths. Sketch below, open to bikeshedding.

Chris Nguyen: Nice! curious how this differs from current global notify-policy? Do we intend to do per-route attenuation + batching?

Samir Rao: Proposed: map route -> {severity, notify_channels, batch_window_ms, backoff_factor}. Batch window 30s for telemetry-only alerts, 0s for latency spike on primary routes.

Lina Gomez: UX note: console needs to surface "expected escalation behavior" per route in the SLO editor. Otherwise PMs will file tickets. We should show simulated timeline.

Maya Patel: Agreed. Also want to add a "suppress if sibling low-priority" rule for churny endpoints. Example config I'm prototyping:

```json
{
  "route": "/api/v1/gen",
  "slo": {
    "target": 0.999,
    "window_days": 7
  },
  "escalation": {
    "severity": "warning",
    "channels": ["ops", "oncall-signal"],
    "batch_ms": 30000,
    "suppress_if_sibling_active": true,
    "backoff": {"initial_ms": 30000, "factor": 2}
  }
}
```

Priya Menon: API shape looks fine. How does this affect alert counts in billing/quotas? We can't silently drop notifications that customers rely on for audit.

Chris Nguyen: We'll still emit telemetry for every raw trigger, but only fanout notifications after batching logic — telemetry count preserved. For billing we can count raw triggers; for oncall load we count fanouts.

ops-bot: [alert] test-alert: route=/api/v1/gen, raw_triggers=12, batched=1, throttled=0

Samir Rao: Implementation detail: prefer a token-bucket style backoff per-route keyed by (org, route, severity). Backoff pseudo:

```
if bucket_tokens > 0:
  send; bucket_tokens -= 1
else:
  enqueue for batch window
bucket_tokens += refill_rate * elapsed_ms
```

Lina Gomez: For the console, add a "what to expect" modal that shows: first notification after X sec, repeated with exponential backoff, and who will be paged (escalation matrix). Also a toggle "suppress gray routes".

Maya Patel: Plan: land backend toggle + API v1/escalation-schema, then UI can surface. Rollout: feature flag for 10% orgs -> 50% -> all with canary on high-SLA customers last. I'll open an RFC and a small UX mock.

Priya Menon: Agree on rollout. Add automated smoke (simulate 200 triggers across 5 routes) and check fanout vs telemetry. Can we add a console-level override to force immediate fanout for audits?

Maya Patel: Yes — add `force_fanout=true` on the alert object; admin-only. I'll include in RFC.

Chris Nguyen: One last ask: add an opt-in "quiet window" for non-business hours per-org. Could be useful to drop paging for low-priority routes.

Maya Patel: +1. I'll include sleep windows and a UI to edit per-tenant windows. Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll publish RFC this afternoon.
